proposals.before: In 1794, when the Qianlong Emperor traveled to Tianjin, Yao placed first in the summoned examination and was appointed an Inner Cabinet secretary, then served as a Grand Council clerk.
proposals.after: In 1794, when the Qianlong Emperor traveled to Tianjin, Yao placed first in the summoned examination and was appointed an Inner Cabinet secretary, serving as a Grand Council clerk.
proposals.reason: Chinese 充 marks concurrent service as Grand Council clerk, not a later sequential posting implied by English then.

proposals.before: Longer terms for governors-general and governors would lighten the tribute counties and districts must supply them; easing the routine charges imposed on local magistrates would allow more capable officials to survive in post."
proposals.after: If governors-general and governors served longer terms, counties and districts would have to supply their establishments less; if the routine charges against county and district magistrates were relaxed, more talented men could be preserved in office."
proposals.reason: The idiomatic sentence is ungrammatical and obscures 供億 (supplying official establishments) as a relative clause without that.

proposals.before: The Qin ruled through draconian law, measuring documents by the stone and scheduling work by the bushel; when one man shouted in the night, rebellion broke out everywhere—because the people were governed through fear alone.
proposals.after: The Qin ruled through draconian law, weighing documents by the stone and assigning them by quota; when one man shouted in the night, rebellion broke out everywhere—because the people were governed through fear alone.
proposals.reason: 衡石程書 refers to weighing and quotaing official documents, not scheduling work by the bushel.

proposals.before: In 1821 the Jiangsu and Zhejiang governors, including Sun Yuting, proposed banning illicit surcharges on grain transport, formally capping collection at eighty percent while tacitly allowing an extra twenty percent.
proposals.after: In 1821 the Jiangsu and Zhejiang governors-general and governors, including Sun Yuting, proposed banning illicit surcharges on grain transport, formally capping collection at eighty percent while tacitly allowing an extra twenty percent.
proposals.reason: 督撫 names both governors-general and governors; the idiomatic rendering flattens the compound to governors only.

proposals.before: Yet officials cannot control the people without wielding these three charges: students with purchased degrees are temporarily stripped of status, ordinary commoners are detained, and release is requested only after they make up payment.
proposals.after: Yet officials cannot control the people without wielding these three charges: licentiates and Imperial Academy students are temporarily stripped of status, ordinary commoners are detained, and release is requested only after they make up payment.
proposals.reason: 生監 denotes shengyuan and jiansheng (government students), not specifically purchasers of degrees.

proposals.before: When the memorial was submitted, the ministry deliberated.
proposals.after: When the memorial was submitted, it was sent down to the ministries for deliberation.
proposals.reason: 下部議 means the memorial was referred downward to the relevant ministries, not that a single ministry simply deliberated.

proposals.before: He served as Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent and Grand Secretary of the Inner Cabinet.
proposals.after: He served as Junior Supervisor of the Household of the Heir Apparent and as a Bachelor of the Grand Secretariat.
proposals.reason: 內閣學士 is a mid-rank academician of the Grand Secretariat, not 大學士 (Grand Secretary); 少詹事 is Junior Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's household rather than a generic tutor.

proposals.before: He served successively as Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent and Grand Secretary of the Inner Cabinet.
proposals.after: He served successively as Junior Supervisor of the Household of the Heir Apparent and as a Bachelor of the Grand Secretariat.
proposals.reason: The literal likewise renders 內閣學士 as Grand Secretary, which names the wrong office.

proposals.before: but lightly reprimanded his father Bin for grading papers while receiving support from his son and for fragmenting examination topics.
proposals.after: but, regarding his father Bin grading papers while receiving support in his son's household, and regarding fragmented examination topics, Shiyan was only lightly reprimanded.
proposals.reason: 薄譴之 takes Shiyan as object; 命題割裂 is an examiner's fault, not Bin's. The edict rebukes Shiyan over both the father's 就養閱卷 and the split topics.

proposals.before: only rebuking his father Bin for receiving support while grading examination papers and for fragmenting examination topics, with a light reprimand.
proposals.after: only rebuking him concerning his father Bin receiving support and grading papers, and concerning fragmented examination topics, with a light reprimand.
proposals.reason: The English makes Bin the reprimanded agent of 命題割裂; the Chinese pairs 斥…及… then 薄譴之 of Shiyan.

proposals.before: The Gaoyan head fort and second and third forts, already estimated but not started, and the Zhi and Xin dams, not yet estimated, should be undertaken immediately.
proposals.after: The Gaoyan first and second forts, already estimated but not started, and the Zhi and Xin dams, not yet estimated, should be undertaken immediately.
proposals.reason: Chinese 高堰頭、二兩堡 means the first (head) and second forts (two forts), not a head fort plus second and third forts.

proposals.before: The Gaoyan head and second and third forts already estimated but not yet undertaken, and the Zhi and Xin dams not yet estimated, should be immediately undertaken.
proposals.after: The Gaoyan head and second forts already estimated but not yet undertaken, and the Zhi and Xin dams not yet estimated, should be immediately undertaken.
proposals.reason: 二兩堡 is the two forts numbered head and second, not three forts.

proposals.before: Ordered with Governor-General Cheng Zuluo to investigate collusion and fraud among gentry, secretaries, and clerks in Shanyin and Kuaiji, he established the facts, secured the dismissal of Acting Provincial Judicial Commissioner Li Yun, and secured varying punishments for other offenders.
proposals.after: Ordered with Governor-General Cheng Zuluo to investigate collusion and fraud among gentry, secretaries, and clerks in Shanyin and Kuaiji, he established the facts, secured the dismissal of Provincial Judicial Commissioner Li Yun (then residing at home), and secured varying punishments for other offenders.
proposals.reason: 在籍按察使 means a judicial commissioner living at his native place, not an acting commissioner.

proposals.before: He was ordered with Governor-General Cheng Zuluo to investigate collusion and fraud among gentry, secretaries, and clerks in Shanyin and Kuaiji; the facts were established, and he requested stripping Acting Provincial Judicial Commissioner Li Yun of office, with other offenders punished by military exile in varying degrees.
proposals.after: He was ordered with Governor-General Cheng Zuluo to investigate collusion and fraud among gentry, secretaries, and clerks in Shanyin and Kuaiji; the facts were established, and he requested stripping the at-home Provincial Judicial Commissioner Li Yun of office, with other offenders punished by military exile in varying degrees.
proposals.reason: 在籍 does not mean acting (署); it means residing in one's native registration.

proposals.before: In 1838 he concurrently served as Shuntian Prefect and presided over the metropolitan examination.
proposals.after: In 1838 he concurrently managed the affairs of the Shuntian Prefect and presided over the metropolitan examination.
proposals.reason: Chinese is 兼管順天府尹事 (concurrently managed the prefect's affairs), matching the literal, not a full appointment as prefect.

proposals.before: Though capital inspection had no explicit rule, he cited precedent of demoted censors nominated as department directors and requested an imperial ruling.
proposals.after: Though capital inspection had no explicit rule, he cited precedent of demoted censors nominated as vice directors and requested an imperial ruling.
proposals.reason: 員外郎 is a vice director (Yuanwailang), not a department director (Langzhong).

proposals.before: He presided over the Guangxi and Yunnan provincial examinations and was transferred to a director in the Imperial Clan Court.
proposals.after: He presided over the Guangxi and Yunnan provincial examinations and was transferred to a secretary in the Imperial Clan Court.
proposals.reason: 宗人府主事 is a secretary (Zhushi), not a director.

proposals.before: He served in the Ministry of War, rose to department director, presided over the Shaanxi-Gansu provincial examination, and was appointed censor and supervising secretary.
proposals.after: He served in the Ministry of War, rose to vice director, presided over the Shaanxi-Gansu provincial examination, and was appointed censor and supervising secretary.
proposals.reason: 員外郎 is vice director, not department director.

proposals.before: He also impeached Supervising Secretary Se Cheng'e, listed for severe punishment in capital inspection yet who argued in person to be downgraded to third class, treating the process as a game; the Censor-in-Chief was severely censured while Se Cheng'e was listed merely as ill.
proposals.after: He also impeached Supervising Secretary Se Cheng'e, first listed among the six methods of capital-inspection dismissal yet who argued in person to be changed to third class, treating the process as a game; the Censor-in-Chief was severely censured while Se Cheng'e was still listed as ill.
proposals.reason: 京察六法 is the six-method dismissal classification, not six punishments.

proposals.before: He also impeached Censorate capital-inspection Supervising Secretary Se Cheng'e, who had first been listed among the six punishments yet came in person to the public hall to argue, seeking to be changed to third class, treating the matter back and forth like child's play; the Censor-in-Chief was severely deliberated upon, yet Se Cheng'e was still listed as having illness.
proposals.after: He also impeached Censorate capital-inspection Supervising Secretary Se Cheng'e, who had first been listed among the six methods yet came in person to the public hall to argue, seeking to be changed to third class, treating the matter back and forth like child's play; the Censor-in-Chief was severely deliberated upon, yet Se Cheng'e was still listed as having illness.
proposals.reason: 六法 here is the Qing jingcha six-method list, not punishments.

proposals.before: He also impeached Tai'an Prefect Yan Lu and Dongchang Prefect Xiong Fang for bribery, ordering the governor to investigate and impeach;
proposals.after: He also impeached Tai'an Prefect Yan Lu and Dongchang Prefect Xiong Fangshou for accepting illicit solicitations, ordering the governor to investigate and impeach;
proposals.reason: Chinese 熊方受 is the personal name Xiong Fangshou; 受请 means accepting solicitations and is not a truncated name Xiong Fang.

proposals.before: He also impeached Tai'an Prefect Yan Lu and Dongchang Prefect Xiong Fang for accepting bribes, ordering the governor to investigate and impeach severely;
proposals.after: He also impeached Tai'an Prefect Yan Lu and Dongchang Prefect Xiong Fangshou for accepting illicit solicitations, ordering the governor to investigate and impeach severely;
proposals.reason: Same name split: 熊方受 is Xiong Fangshou; 受请 is the charge.

proposals.before: Zong Shi Engui, courtesy name Xiaoshan, was of the Bordered Blue Banner.
proposals.after: Imperial clansman Engui, courtesy name Xiaoshan, was of the Bordered Blue Banner.
proposals.reason: 宗室 marks imperial-clan status, not a surname Zong Shi.

proposals.before: Through nine promotions he reached Grand Secretary of the Inner Cabinet and Vice Commander-in-Chief.
proposals.after: Through nine promotions he reached Academician of the Inner Cabinet, concurrently Vice Commander-in-Chief.
proposals.reason: 內閣學士 is a cabinet academician, not Grand Secretary (大學士).

proposals.before: Through nine promotions he reached Grand Secretary of the Inner Cabinet, concurrently serving as Vice Commander-in-Chief.
proposals.after: Through nine promotions he reached Academician of the Inner Cabinet, concurrently serving as Vice Commander-in-Chief.
proposals.reason: 內閣學士 is not Grand Secretary.

proposals.before: Absent from six civil office sessions, he was demoted to Grand Secretary of the Inner Cabinet.
proposals.after: Absent from six civil office sessions, he was demoted to Academician of the Inner Cabinet.
proposals.reason: Demotion is to 內閣學士, not Grand Secretary.

proposals.before: Because he was absent from six sessions of civil office, he was demoted to Grand Secretary of the Inner Cabinet.
proposals.after: Because he was absent from six sessions of civil office, he was demoted to Academician of the Inner Cabinet.
proposals.reason: Demotion is to 內閣學士, not Grand Secretary.

proposals.before: When four hundred Old Summer Palace guards were added, he was ordered with Minister Saishanga to train them.
proposals.after: When four hundred Old Summer Palace garden workmen were added, he was ordered with Minister Saishanga to train them.
proposals.reason: 園丁 are garden workmen of Yuanmingyuan, not guards.

proposals.before: When Zhejiang Military Commissioner Yu Buyun bungled coastal defense, he was arrested, interrogated, and punished.
proposals.after: When Zhejiang Provincial Commander Yu Buyun bungled coastal defense, he was arrested, interrogated, and punished.
proposals.reason: 浙江提督 is the provincial commander (tidu), not a commissioner.

proposals.before: He impeached Sacrifices Vice Director Feng Shen and granary Censor Guang Hu for dereliction and dismissed both.
proposals.after: He impeached Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Feng Shen and the granary-inspection Censor Guang Hu for dereliction of duty, and both were dismissed.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English fuses the office into the opaque phrase Sacrifices Vice Director and makes Engui personally dismiss them; the Chinese has 太常寺丞 and 並罷之 as the resulting dismissals.

proposals.before: He died in office in 1848; the Emperor deeply mourned him, praising his willingness to bear hardship and his wholehearted dedication; he was posthumously titled Grand Preceptor Wensu, with gold granted for his funeral.
proposals.after: He died in office in 1848; the Emperor deeply mourned him, praising his willingness to bear hardship and resentment and his wholehearted dedication; he was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor, given gold for the funeral, and posthumously titled Wensu.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English fuses 贈太保 and 諡文肅 into a single title Grand Preceptor Wensu and drops 任怨.

decisions.reason: 充軍機章京 marks filling the Grand Council clerkship together with the Inner Cabinet secretaryship, not a later sequential posting implied by then.
